pass_meta.note: 2 Nov 2026 update pass: parked WO Board tests whose tickets are Done, retested on production

observed: The drag to another technician shows "<number> assigned to <technician>" with an Undo button.
The drag to Unassigned shows "<number> moved to Unassigned" with an Undo button.
Each message closes by itself about 5 seconds after it appears, without being clicked.
Clicking the current lead in the dialog closes the dialog.
No lead-change message appears in the 10 seconds after.
The lead stays the same, Line 2 still reads Unassigned and the work order history gains no entry.
With Assigned to me on, the dialog still offers the technicians whose columns are not on screen.
The dialog has only Cancel, no confirm button; clicking a technician assigns them at once.
The work order leaves the board without a reload, and the board shows "No work orders match these filters", "Try removing a filter to widen your results." and a Clear all filters button.
Tab from Search reaches the first card in Unassigned; the arrow keys move the focus ring card to card.
Tab reaches the card's More actions button; Enter opens the menu with Reassign lead technician and Unassign.
Typing in the dialog narrows the list; arrow keys and Enter assign the technician, with the message and Undo.
Unassign chosen with the keyboard moves the work order to Unassigned, with "<number> moved to Unassigned" and Undo.
The drag to another technician opens "Clear <technician>'s scheduled shifts?" with Cancel, Keep Shifts, Clear Shifts and a close X.
Cancel, the X and Escape each call the change off: the card goes back to its lead, no message appears.
From the dialog route, Cancel takes you back to the Reassign lead technician dialog with nothing changed.
The same in Tech View. At the end the lead is unchanged and the 8:00-12:00 shift is still on the Schedule.
The card's menu offers Assign lead technician (the work order has no lead).
Clicking the technician assigns at once, with "<number> assigned to <technician>" and Undo.
Line 1 (no technician) now follows the new lead; Line 2 keeps its own technician; Line 3 (Complete) stays Unassigned.
Each of the three drags opens "Clear <technician>'s scheduled shifts?": the line not approved and the declined line are ignored, and a Choose lines shift ticking every approved line counts.
After Keep shifts each work order moves, each with its own "<number> assigned to <technician>" message and Undo.
All three shifts are still on the Schedule tomorrow at the same times.
The drag to another technician shows the message with Undo, closing by itself after about 5 seconds; the work order page then shows that technician as lead.
The drag to Unassigned shows "<number> moved to Unassigned"; the page then shows no lead technician.
The drag out of Unassigned assigns the new column's technician; in Tech View the row moves to the new group and the page shows that lead.
Invoiced, Paid and Declined cards show a lock; hovering it reads "Invoiced · can't be reassigned", "Paid · can't be reassigned" and "Declined · can't be reassigned". The Approved card has none.
The Invoiced card can be reordered within its technician's column.
Dropping Invoiced, Paid or Declined cards on another technician or on Unassigned is refused: the note shows at the top of that column, the card stays, no message, the count is unchanged.
The Invoiced card with no lead cannot leave Unassigned; the Complete card moves with its message and Undo; Tech View follows the same rule.
Same run as C97009 (this is its release copy): every lock, tooltip, refused drop with its note, the reorder within the technician and the Tech View rule behave as written.
The Complete card moves to the other technician.
After the drag from Unassigned the message is the design's white message with the green check icon, rounded with a soft shadow, reading "<number> assigned to <technician>" with an Undo button.
It is not the app's standard success message.
It closes by itself about 5 seconds after it appears.
